title: On Staring at the closed door for a minute
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：stare　|　正文 370 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 stare 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the operator ① stared at the closed door for a minute on the same day, and every trainee in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the operator ② stares at the closed door for a minute before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ stare at the closed door for a minute at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ stared at the closed door for a minute before — a line in the log for June 1947 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Staring at the closed door for a minute on the same day, the operator said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ stare out of the window all afternoon before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Stare out of the window all afternoon at once and never mention it again.

By 1960 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the log, and a new trainee from the next station ⑧ stares out of the window all afternoon on the same day every shift without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the screen, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ stared at the closed door for a minute again when nobody else would.

⑩ To stare at the closed door for a minute, my mother said in 1965, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody stares at the closed door for a minute before dawn again and somebody must stare at the closed door for a minute on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 凝视（一般过去式 stared at the closed door for a minute：1953 年操作员头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 凝视（一般现在 stares at the closed door for a minute：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 凝视（不定式 to stare at the closed door for a minute：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 凝视（过去完成时 had stared at the closed door for a minute：1947 年六月的运行日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 凝视（动名词 staring at the closed door for a minute 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 盯着看（stare out of the window all afternoon：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去盯着看整个下午盯着窗外）
G. v. 盯着看（stare out of the window all afternoon：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 凝视（后段两处：新来的实习生照例 stares out of the window all afternoon，而母亲又一次 stared at the closed door for a minute）

answers.why: stare 意为“凝视”，1953 年操作员当天就凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿，那是机房里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 stared。
stare 意为“凝视”，自那以后操作员天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 stares。
stare 意为“凝视”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿”，此处为不定式 to stare at the closed door for a minute。
stare 意为“凝视”，运行日志里 六月 那行字说明早在 1960 年之前就有人凝视过，故用过去完成时 had stared。
stare 意为“凝视”，操作员说“凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 staring at the closed door for a minute 作主语。
stare 意为“盯着看”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去盯着看整个下午盯着窗外”，should ever 之后用原形 stare out of the window all afternoon。
stare 意为“盯着看”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻盯着看整个下午盯着窗外（stare out of the window all afternoon at once），以后再也不要提起。
stare 意为“凝视”，新来的实习生每个班次都照例盯着看整个下午盯着窗外，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 stares。
stare 意为“凝视”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿，用一般过去式 stared 叙述。
stare 意为“凝视”，结尾那句是母亲 1965 年的话：要凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和机房记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1953 年，操作员当天就凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿；机房里每一个实习生都说这是头一回。（stared at the closed door for a minute）
多年以后，操作员仍天没亮就做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（stares at the closed door for a minute）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿这件事本身。（to stare at the closed door for a minute）
早在 1947 年就有人凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿，六月那天运行日志上的一行字就是证据。（had stared at the closed door for a minute）
操作员说过，当天就凝视对着那扇关着的门看了一会儿这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（staring at the closed door for a minute 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻盯着看整个下午盯着窗外，以后再也不要提起。（stare out of the window all afternoon，祈使句）
answers: In 1953 the operator stared at the closed door for a minute on the same day, and every trainee in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three shifts on, the operator still stares at the closed door for a minute before dawn without being asked.
My mother said later that to stare at the closed door for a minute at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had stared at the closed door for a minute long before 1960, and the line in the log for June proves it.
Staring at the closed door for a minute on the same day, the operator said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Stare out of the window all afternoon at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 stare 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1953 the operator stared at the closed door for a minute on the same day, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the operator stares at the closed door for a minute before dawn whenever the station asks.
Staring at the closed door for a minute on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever stare out of the window all afternoon before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new trainee from the next station stares out of the window all afternoon on the same day every shift, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother stared at the closed door for a minute again, and the station remembered that half.
